 Heat must stick with Myron Gardner even when Pelle Larsson makes his return 
 Myron Gardner has been a lightning rod for the Heat. By Michael Saenz | Nov 16, 2026, 8:15 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Miami Heat forward Myron Gardner (15) reacts (Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect To a certain extent, Myron Gardner's entry into the Miami Heat's rotation over the last couple of games was triggered by Klay Thompson's injury and Pelle Larsson's absence due to an illness. However, even as he prepares to make his return, and now that Klay is back , Erik Spoelstra needs to find a way to keep the energetic wing in the rotation. 
--> To a certain extent, Myron Gardner's entry into the Miami Heat's rotation over the last couple of games was triggered by Klay Thompson's injury and Pelle Larsson's absence due to an illness. However, even as he prepares to make his return, and now that Klay is back , Erik Spoelstra needs to find a way to keep the energetic wing in the rotation. 
 Just taking a quick glance at the stat sheet, there may not be much that backs up this narrative. However, when you look a bit deeper than just the five points scored, it's easy to realize his true value for this team. 
--> Just taking a quick glance at the stat sheet, there may not be much that backs up this narrative. However, when you look a bit deeper than just the five points scored, it's easy to realize his true value for this team. 
 It's not just the nine rebounds, three assists, or two blocks either. Gardner's greatest value to the Heat revolves around his infectious energy, effort, and hustle that he brings every time he checks into the game. 
--> It's not just the nine rebounds, three assists, or two blocks either. Gardner's greatest value to the Heat revolves around his infectious energy, effort, and hustle that he brings every time he checks into the game. 
 Myron Gardner brings an infectious brand of energy that the Heat needs

 Sometimes, especially for supporting cast characters, it's those small intangibles, which are often overlooked, that end up making the biggest difference for a team. During the Heat's roughest stretch of the season, the Heat needed Gardner's energy to help spark the team.
--> Sometimes, especially for supporting cast characters, it's those small intangibles, which are often overlooked, that end up making the biggest difference for a team. During the Heat's roughest stretch of the season, the Heat needed Gardner's energy to help spark the team.
 That's exactly what he helped do as Miami pulled off two of their most impressive wins on back-to-back nights of the season thus far. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo made all the headlines, and rightfully so , but I'm not sure if Miami would have won both of those games without the contributions of a player like Gardner, especially as he was asked to step in with Klay out against Cleveland and with Larsson missing the last two. 
--> That's exactly what he helped do as Miami pulled off two of their most impressive wins on back-to-back nights of the season thus far. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo made all the headlines, and rightfully so , but I'm not sure if Miami would have won both of those games without the contributions of a player like Gardner, especially as he was asked to step in with Klay out against Cleveland and with Larsson missing the last two. 
 So even with Larsson likely back within the next few days, it'd be increasingly shocking if Spoelstra didn't find a path to keeping Gardner in the rotation. Theoretically speaking, it likely would have to come at the expense of Tim Hardaway Jr., who has been completely cut out of the rotation in two of the Heat's last three games. 
--> So even with Larsson likely back within the next few days, it'd be increasingly shocking if Spoelstra didn't find a path to keeping Gardner in the rotation. Theoretically speaking, it likely would have to come at the expense of Tim Hardaway Jr., who has been completely cut out of the rotation in two of the Heat's last three games. 
 These are the difficult decisions that Spoelstra has to make, but if Gardner is the more valuable player on the team, the move is simple. And right now, especially as Hardaway Jr. continues to search for his shooting touch, Gardner is just the more valuable contributor to the Heat. 
--> These are the difficult decisions that Spoelstra has to make, but if Gardner is the more valuable player on the team, the move is simple. And right now, especially as Hardaway Jr. continues to search for his shooting touch, Gardner is just the more valuable contributor to the Heat. 
 In a very unexpected way, some of the Heat's early-season struggles may have led Spoelstra to the right rotation. At least for now, Gardner needs to be included in it. That could change, but especially with how he's played recently, it'd be a big mistake to pull him out now.
